A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HeatFormer research. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and figures, and corresponding material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original HeatFormer benchmark results, cross-dataset evaluations, occlusion experiments, qualitative reconstructions, and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds calibration comparisons, component ablations, additional iteration configurations, and BEHAVE baseline results.

M1.justification: The HeatEncoder, iterative decoder, view-dependent SMPL outputs, and training losses remain unchanged. Bypassing AdaFuse and regressing weak-perspective camera parameters for uncalibrated inputs already appear in v1 Section 3.3. Additional iteration configurations do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Human3.6M, MPI-INF-3DHP, BEHAVE, RICH, and the mesh-recovery task are retained. v3 adds explicit four-view evaluation without camera extrinsics in Appendix D/Table A, extending the calibration conditions beyond v1's explicitly described calibration-free single-view evaluation.

E2.justification: The central BEHAVE comparison in Table 6 expands from HMR2.0a/b to also include ProHMR and HMR2.0a/b+ScoreHMR. This introduces multiview refinement comparators into the occlusion/generalization evaluation, substantially strengthening that comparison. The comparator sets in the other main benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds four-iteration configurations to Tables 2, 3, and 6, extends the iteration study from one–three to one–five iterations, and introduces calibration and component-replacement controls. Existing dataset splits, metrics, BEHAVE joint filters, training schedules, and loss weights remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses compare calibrated versus uncalibrated operation, replace the decoder with pooling plus an MLP, and replace heatmaps with joint-coordinate tokens (Tables A, D, and F). The iteration study gains four- and five-iteration models. These directly test important architectural and applicability questions beyond the retained HeatEncoder, image-feature, spatial-pooling, and view-aggregation ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained BEHAVE joint-confidence thresholds are evaluation filters, not uncertainty estimates for the reported results.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and 6 revise existing scores: three-iteration Human3.6M MPJPE changes from 30.3 to 30.7, and MPI-INF-3DHP MPJPE from 39.3 to 39.8. Four-iteration results and new appendix controls add substantial findings. Newly included HMR2.0a+ScoreHMR achieves lower PA-MPJPE than HeatFormer under both BEHAVE protocols, while HeatFormer retains lower MPJPE. Tables 5, 7, and 8 retain their values.

T1.justification: The SMPL and heatmap definitions and loss equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced; the added validation is empirical.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly foregrounds calibration independence in the abstract and introduction, whereas v1's abstract specifies calibrated cameras. This broadens the stated main applicability claim, although uncalibrated operation was already described in v1's method. The central neural-optimization, robustness, and generalization contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets calibration information as improving accuracy while uncalibrated operation remains usable. It revises the convergence discussion from three iterations to three or four. BEHAVE discussion also changes from claiming 'higher' accuracy to 'high' accuracy alongside the expanded comparison.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies that the iteration ablation compares separately trained models and explains where camera extrinsics are used. It replaces the laboratory homepage with a project-specific link and removes the promise to release code and data upon acceptance. Hardware, preprocessing, optimizer settings, and training times remain unchanged; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Vision Transformer paper by Dosovitskiy et al.; the other cited works are retained. It also removes the discussion excluding U-HMR from the state-of-the-art comparison because of its arXiv-only status. The broader related-work organization and first-neural-optimizer positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section structure and most prose are retained. Changes comprise localized wording corrections, clearer calibration explanations, revised experimental discussion, and a new Calibration appendix section that shifts Ablation Study from Appendix D to E.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 6 gain rows; the appendix gains three new tables and an expanded iteration table. Existing appendix tables and the decoder diagram move, and appendix figures/tables receive letter labels. Visual inspection confirms that the existing qualitative figures and architecture illustrations are retained, with local layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already extensive evaluation with direct decoder and heatmap controls, multiview refinement baselines on BEHAVE, and evidence quantifying the cost of operating without calibration. These additions make the central claims easier to assess. Gains remain incremental, and unexplained score revisions—including differing three-iteration reference values in Table 2 versus Tables A/F—still limit reporting clarity.
